target_customer: AI data center operators, hyperscalers and crypto-mining infrastructure operators
problem: Dense compute needs cooling that wastes power and water; air and many liquid systems are complex, capital intensive or need facility redesign.
business_model: Hardware sales of rack-integrated cooling systems, with pilots; revenue not disclosed
product_category: Data center liquid cooling hardware (Adaptive Phase Cooling)

founders.name: Reza Azizian
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page. Over 10 years in electronic cooling.

founders.name: Matteo Bucci
prior_employers: CEA Paris (research scientist, nearly a decade)
founders.background_notes: MIT faculty member in Nuclear Science and Engineering; heat transfer and reactor design. Source: YC company page.

competitors.name: Green Revolution Cooling (GRC)
competitors.what: Single-phase liquid immersion cooling for data centers
competitors.traction_then: Deployed in 13 countries with HPC and crypto mining customers; Dell and HPE agreements
competitors.funding_then: 7 million dollars Series B in July 2020, 15 million total

technical_complexity.rationale: Phase-change heat transfer engineering borrowed from nuclear systems, a proprietary dielectric fluid and rack-level integration are hardware and research-heavy for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Deep thermal physics expertise and proprietary fluid and hardware design are hard to copy, though immersion cooling is a crowded field.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established and funded immersion cooling companies kept growing; no acquisition of Ferveret found.

market_need_then: Crypto mining and HPC were already adopting immersion cooling in 2020 (GRC customers), and AI compute density later increased demand. The CEO traces the idea to 2017.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and mission-led: cooling that scales without scaling emissions

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage from MIT News and tech outlets about the nuclear-inspired approach; no community found. A trademark application for FERVERET was filed on 2023-10-10 per a trademark record.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive name with technology-story coverage, but a B2B hardware brand with little visibility so far.

pivots.from: Liquid immersion cooling for data centers and ASIC digital-asset infrastructure
pivots.to: Adaptive Phase Cooling for AI data centers
pivots.why: The older company site lists data center and digital-asset lines; the YC page and 2026 coverage focus on AI data centers. Date not sourced.

outcome_analysis: Ferveret is an MIT-linked hardware company applying reactor heat transfer ideas to AI data center cooling. It raised a seed round described as about 10 million dollars from investors including Aramco Ventures and Y Combinator and ran pilots with data center operators, and it is moving toward a Series A. The AI compute boom is a tailwind, while the outcome depends on converting pilots into purchases against funded rivals.
notes: Funding conflict: Seedtable (aggregator) lists a 2.1 million dollar seed in September 2021 and totals of 2.13 to 2.23 million; the CEO interview on Pulse 2 (October 2026) says roughly 10 million in seed from a named syndicate. The 10 million figure is recorded as a round with no date because the source gives none; the 2.1 million figure is unverified. Two other aggregators differ again (Caplight 9.83 million). The older company website still lists San Jose and immersion lines. Other immersion competitors (LiquidStack, Submer) had no source dated near 2021 in the results, so they are not listed. The name origin was not found; the Latin root is not sourced.
